title: Release contracts and offline rollback cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook / cheatsheet for private (VPC / air-gapped / on-prem) release mechanics. Focus: defining the release contract between build pipelines, Terraform operator modules, and GitOps (Argo) apps so teams can do safe upgrades and fast offline rollbacks.

Scope / When to use this:
- Performing canary or staged upgrades for private customers
- Promoting signed images/artifact bundles into air-gapped registries
- Rolling back safely when smoke tests or SLIs degrade
- Updating Terraform module inputs that affect image provenance or KMS keys

High-level principles (short):
1) Always sign images/artifacts with cosign and include SBOM + provenance. Enforce verification in the cluster before deploy.
2) Treat the Terraform module interface as a contract: don't change variable names or required outputs without a major version bump.
3) Push minimal, observable rollouts: small canaries, automated smoke tests, and an explicit rollback path.
4) Keep an offline artifact bundle for each release (OCI blobs, SBOM, attestations, helm chart tarball).

Preflight checks (pipeline):
- Build pipeline produces: image digest, cosign signature, attestation (predicate), SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX), helm-chart.tgz, and manifest-commit SHA.
- Run artifact validation: sbom-validator, cosign verify --keyless OR --key, and attestations-checker.
- Generate release-bundle: bundle.tar.gz with a manifest.json listing: image:digest, chart:version, sbom:path, attestations:path.
- Publish bundle to staging registry or OCI proxy for airgap ingestion.

Terraform module contract (recommended interface - keep stable):
- variables (API):
  - required_image_registry (string)  # endpoint teams will deploy from
  - release_bundle_prefix (string)   # S3/OCI prefix where archive is stored for offline import
  - image_signature_key_ref (string) # KMS/HSM key id for signature verification policy
  - allowed_schemas (list)           # e.g. ["spdx","cyclonedx"]
  - gitops_app_repo (string)         # repo containing Argo app manifests

- outputs (API):
  - images_verified (string)         # last verified image:digest
  - bundle_manifest_url (string)     # canonical link used in release notes
  - kms_policy_version (string)

Notes on changing the contract: any rename or type change requires module semver bump and a migration guide in the module repo. Keep the module tests that validate the outputs (images_verified, bundle_manifest_url).

GitOps (Argo) patterns:
- App-per-env, image-digest pinning: manifests should pin container images by digest (not tag). Example: image: ghcr.io/org/redwood-inference/model-server@sha256:abcd
- Argo Application manifest should include syncPolicy: automated with prune=false for private deployments, and allowEmpty=true only for maintenance windows.
- Canary strategy: use two Argo apps (app-stable, app-canary) or a single app with kustomize overlays for canary namespace. Keep canary capacity < 10% unless explicit SLA tests pass.
- Sync waves: for multi-component releases, use sync-wave annotations so core infra updates (CRDs, operator) occur before app rollouts.

Image signing & attestation flow (cosign focused):
1) Build: docker build -> push to internal registry -> get digest
2) Sign: cosign sign -key ksm://projects/... OR cosign sign-blob --key $(KMS_KEY)   (CI holds signing perms)
3) Attest: use cosign attest -predicate sbom.json -key ... to produce attestation payload for provenance collector
4) Upload SBOM and attestations to bundle storage and include references in bundle manifest.json
5) In-cluster: admission controller (Gatekeeper/OPA or a lightweight mutating webhook) runs cosign verify on incoming images and checks attestation predicates against allowed provenance.

Commands (examples):
- Sign image (CI):
  cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/release-key \\n    ghcr.io/redwood/model-server@sha256:$DIGEST

- Verify (cluster / dev):
  cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/release-key ghcr.io/redwood/model-server@sha256:$DIGEST

- Generate SBOM (example):
  syft ghcr.io/redwood/model-server:$TAG -o spdx-json > sbom.json

Airgap artifact bundle recipe (brief):
- Create directory: release-$VERSION/
  - chart/model-server-$VERSION.tgz
  - images/list.txt (image:sha256 lines)
  - sboms/*.json
  - attestations/*.json
  - manifest.json (small index)
- Sign the bundle itself (cosign sign-blob bundle.tar.gz) and include signature alongside.
- Provide an ingestion script for customers: import-bundle.sh that loads images into private registry and registers the chart.

Upgrade & canary checklist (pipeline + runbook):
1) Create release bundle and verify artifacts.
2) Create GitOps commit pointing at new image digests and chart tarball URL (bundle). Open PR against customer/cluster overlays.
3) CI runs preflight e2e + smoke tests in an isolated staging cluster (same K8s version if possible).
4) Merge PR to canary branch -> Argo picks up app-canary.
5) Monitor for N minutes (configurable, default 20m): health checks, error budget, tail-latency, CPU/GC anomalies.
6) If pass, promote to stable branch or update app-stable commit. If fail, trigger automated rollback and create hotfix PR.

Rollback mechanics (fast offline rollback):
- Prepare: Always keep last 3 stable bundle archives available in the artifact store (or in customer’s airgap bundle cache).
- Triggering rollback: three sources
  - Automated: CI smoke tests or SLO monitors trigger a rollback job via the operator or Argo CLI.
  - Manual (SRE): runbook command: argocd app rollback model-server <REVISION> OR git revert commit and push to repo to trigger Argo to sync.
  - Airgapped manual: run import-bundle.sh for the desired stable bundle, update overlay commit to the pinned digest, and push patch to customer repo (or run operator API).

Argo rollback example (hosted control plane access):
- Check history: argocd app history model-server --refresh
- Rollback by revision: argocd app rollback model-server 3 --hard
- Force resync: argocd app sync model-server --force

Helm patterns during upgrade/rollback:
- Use helm upgrade --atomic --wait --timeout 5m for hosted maintenance. For private deployments where helm is controlled via GitOps, ensure the chart repository URL points to the bundle and the values.yaml pins image digests.
- Keep chart hooks minimal; prefer Kubernetes-native readiness/liveness probes to surface failures early.

Gating & admission policies:
- OPA/Gatekeeper constraint example: require cio.signatureVerified == true and cio.sbomHash in allowedSBOMs for release bundle
- Admission flow: ImageAdmissionWebhook -> cosign verify -> attestations verifier -> allow/deny

Observability & signals (what to watch):
- App-level: 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, request success rate, queue size for model server
- Infra-level: pod restart count, OOMKill, node pressure, kubelet errors
- Pipeline-level: verification failures (cosign verify), bundle ingest errors, terraform apply drift

Emergency hotfix & fast patch pattern:
- If a critical bug is found in a release, create a patch branch from stable, build minimal image, sign it, create a minimal bundle, and push a fast-forward PR to the repo. Avoid schema changes to Terraform module variables or CRD upgrades in hotfixes.

Postmortem and artifact retention:
- Retain release bundles + signatures and SBOMs for 90 days minimum; prefer 1 year for regulated/private customers.
- For each rollback, record: triggering metric, operator action, bundle IDs for before/after, and timeline in incident doc.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting tips
- Argo not syncing? Check repo credentials and repo-server logs, then argocd app get <app> for last error.
- cosign verify failing in-cluster but passing in CI? Check KMS key access from the cluster service-account and time skew with HSM.
- Airgap ingest failing on registry push: confirm manifest lists/OCI blob layers are present and that the customer registry accepts digest uploads (some registries require special flags).

Open questions / TODOs (team):
- Standardize the bundle manifest JSON schema across engineering and solutions so ingestion tooling is shared.
- Add automated terraform module integration tests that validate upgrading KMS policy and image_signature_key_ref without downtime.
- Evaluate use of supply-chain attestation frameworks beyond cosign (in-toto connectors).

-- end of cheatsheet --
